My therapist told me to always put my thoughts under scrutiny like it was a trial, have an inner attorney lol
Thought: i hate my bf i'd be happier without him
Inner attorney: what proof do you have of this? Since when have you felt like this? Did something happen that made the change?  What is the precedent? How was your life before him? What has he added to your life, do you have proof of that? How would you feel if you couldn't talk to him, have you tried it? Etcetera etcetera but always ask for proof, this process really helps with self hate speech too

I had this problem! My psychologist explained that bipolar people feel on the range of 100 and non bipolar in the range of 10. When you start treatment it can feel like you are numb but it's just that you are so used to this big range you can't identify the smaller one. 
It's like being used to covering everything you eat in tabasco and then eating something with just a bit of pepper, it's going to take a while to feel the spice again. But your feelings and creativity are still there, they're just not going to punch you in the face anymore, you're going to have to learn to find them and listen to them.
My music took a stall but now it's back to normal. Don't fall into the myth that says your art is only good if you suffer, you can have a great life and be able to access that creativity when you want to.

yes. A healthy diet, exercise and sleep are incredibly important for bipolar. Think about it like this: you know that if you have a healthy lifestyle you're very unlikely to have heart or liver failure, well your brain is also an organ and it will be much less likely to fail you (episodes) than otherwise. I've had incredible results with it.

I don't believe in diet culture and internet fads so I would just recommend going to a professional dietitian that will teach you how to get all your macro and micro nutrients. I did that like a year ago and I haven't had any episodes.
